metadata.architecture: width-2 residual causal attention bottleneck with tied readout
metadata.author: anadim, declarative experiment wrapper
metadata.mechanism_hypothesis: A single narrow residual attention path can preserve eligibility while eliminating parameters from depth routing, feed-forward layers, learned positions, and normalization.
metadata.name: Compact Residual Attention AdderBoard Decoder
metadata.research_current_explanation: The model retains a direct token-and-position path while one causal attention operation supplies prefix-dependent carry information.
metadata.research_evidence: The visible control executed successfully, was transformer-valid and eligible, but had public accuracy 0.0. There is therefore no public evidence that its additional decoder depth improved task accuracy.
metadata.research_next_experiment: Replace the routed two-block decoder with a width-2, one-head, sinusoidal residual attention bottleneck tied directly to the readout.
metadata.research_expected_result: The candidate should preserve execution and transformer eligibility with a substantially lower trusted parameter count; its residual path may also ease optimization relative to the deeper control.
metadata.research_decision_rule: Retain if the public eligibility threshold is preserved and the trusted parameter count decreases; use public accuracy only to distinguish equal-size eligible architectures.
metadata.research_previous_interpretation: The conventional causal decoder was structurally valid and eligible, but its 0.0 public accuracy did not demonstrate a benefit from added depth.
